questions.q: In which of the following years did Japan invade India resulting in the Battle of Imphal?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1944.

• In 1944, Japan invade India resulting in the Battle of Imphal.

Key Points

• The Battle of Imphal took place from March to July 1944 in the vicinity of the city of Imphal, the capital of the state of Manipur in northeastern India.

• Japanese forces attempted to destroy the Allied forces at Imphal and invade India, but were driven back to Burma with heavy losses.

• Together with the Battle of Kohima on the road, by which the Allied forces at Imphal were relieved, the battle was the turning point of the Burma Campaign, which was part of the South-East Asian Theater of World War II.

• The defeats at Kohima and Imphal were the largest defeats to date in Japanese history, with many Japanese deaths from hunger, disease and exhaustion during their retreat.

Additional Information

• The operation to take Imphal was named U-go by the Japanese Army.

• It consisted of elements from the 31st Infantry Division of the Japanese Army and as well as units from the Indian National Army, who were in primarily support and scouting roles.

• The Japanese Army crossed into India on the night of 7th March and engaged the British Indian forces guarding the frontiers the morning of 8th March 1944.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Magnetic flux is a vector quantity.
Two magnetic field lines may intersect.
The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.
Earth's magnetic poles coincide with the geographic poles.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is zero.

Key Points

• The net magnetic flux through any closed surface will be zero.

Additional Information

• Gauss' Law for Magnetism:

• Gauss' Law for magnetism applies to the magnetic flux through a closed surface. In this case, the area vector points out from the surface.

• Because magnetic field lines are continuous loops, all closed surfaces have as many magnetic field lines going in as coming out. Hence, the net magnetic flux through a closed surface is zero.

• Net flux = ∫ B • dA = 0

• Gauss' Law for charges was a very useful method for calculating electric fields in highly symmetric situations.

• Gauss' Law for magnetism is considerably less useful, but we'll come up with another law that enables us to calculate magnetic fields in highly symmetric situations.

Magnetic flux:

• Magnetic flux is defined as the number of magnetic field lines passing through a given closed surface.

• It provides the measurement of the total magnetic field that passes through a given surface area.

• It is a scalar quantity.

• The SI unit of magnetic flux is Weber (Wb).

​Magnetic flux associated with any area is given as,

⇒ ϕB = BAcosθ

Where ϕB = magnetic flux, B = magnetic field intensity, A = area, and θ = angle between B and A

questions.q: Plants grown at which of the following places take up carbon dioxide during the night?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Desert.

• Plants grown in Desert places take up carbon dioxide during the night.

Key Points

• The desert plants which grow in semi-arid conditions fix atmospheric CO₂ to form malic acid in the dark.

• These plants accumulate organic acid intermediate during the night to be used during the daytime.

• This pathway is called Crassulacean acid metabolism (CAM) and the plants which carry out crassulacean metabolism are termed CAM plants.

Additional Information

• Different Parts of a Plant: A detailed description of each of the parts of plants is mentioned below:

• Roots: Roots are the most important part of a plant as they are responsible for transferring the necessary nutrients to the plant. They are the agents responsible for delivering water and minerals to the plants.

• Stems: Stems are also support systems for the plants. Their main function is to act as delivery agents for the nutrients and water stored in the roots and transfer them to the other plant parts in the form of glucose.

• Leaves: Leaves are a fundamental part of a plant as all the necessary food for the plants are stored in the leaves.

• Flowers: Flowers are known as the reproductive products of plants. They are mostly responsible for producing fruits.

• Fruits: Fruits are the products of reproduction in plants. The most essential component from which reproduction starts, that is the seed, is present in the fruit.

• Seeds: Seeds are the main agents for reproduction. They can be found most commonly in fruits from where they germinate and develop into new plants.

• They often grow in saline swamps, so breathing roots come out of the water to consume oxygen.

Given:

∠ACB = 102°

Concept Used:

When a quadrilateral is inscribed in a circle, the opposite angles of it are supplementary angles.

The angle subtended at the center is always double the angle subtended at the remaining arc.

The radius from the center of the circle to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line.

Calculation:



Point D is taken on the major arc of the circle. Then, A & D, B & D, C & B, and A & C are joined.

∠ACB = 102°

Now,

∠ADB = (180 – 102)° = 78°

Now,

∠AOB = (78 × 2)° = 156°

Since OA = OB, ΔAOB is an isosceles triangle and ∠OBA = ∠OAB.

Now,

∠AOB + ∠OBA + ∠OAB = 180°

⇒ 2 × ∠OBA = (180 – 156)°

⇒ ∠OBA = 12°

Now,

∠OBA = 12°

∠OAB = 12°

Now,

∠OAP = ∠OAB + ∠BAP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠BAP

⇒ ∠BAP = 78°

Now,

∠OBP = ∠OBA + ∠ABP

⇒ 90° = 12° + ∠ABP

⇒ ∠ABP = 78°

Now,

∠APB + ∠ABP + ∠BAP = 180°

⇒ ∠APB + 78° + 78° = 180°

⇒ ∠APB = 180° - (2 × 78)°

⇒ ∠APB = 24°

questions.q:
Select the option that will substitute the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no substitution is needed, select ‘No substitution required’.

When I met the couple yesterday I noticed that the wife was more taller than her husband.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4) i.e., 'taller'.

Key Points

• The underlined part is grammatically incorrect.

• Taller is a comparative form of the adjective tall.

• We cannot use more before it.

• Hence, option 4 is the correct answer.

Additional Information

• For one syllable adjectives

• add -er for the comparative and -est for the superlative.

• If the adjective has a consonant + single vowel + consonant spelling, the final consonant must be doubled before adding the ending.

• Examples - tall - taller -tallest; big - bigger -biggest

• For two syllables adjectives

• ​form the comparative either by adding -er or by preceding the adjective with more.

• These adjectives form the superlative either by adding -est or by preceding the adjective with most.

• Examples - happy - happier -happiest; tangled - more tangled - most tangled

• For three or more syllables adjectives

• form the comparative by putting more in front of the adjective, and the superlative by putting most in front.

• Examples - important - more important - most important

questions.q:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

Sneha said to me, “I was watching TV.”
options: Sneha told me that she was watching TV.
Sneha said to me that I was watching TV.
Sneha told me that she had been watching TV.
Sneha told me that I was watching TV.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option3) i.e., 'Sneha told methat she had been watching TV.'

Key Points

• The given sentence is an assertive sentence.

• While changing the narration of an assertive sentence, we need to follow steps

• The reporting verb said is changed to told.

• The conjunction 'that' is used in place of commas and inverted commas.

• The first person 'I' will be changed into 'she' and the first person 'me' will be unchanged.

• The verb (was watching) is in the past continuous tense form in the given sentence.

• This changes to past perfect continuous form (had been watching) in the indirect speech.

• Eventually, we will get the final sentence- " Sneha told me that she had been watching TV."

• Hence, option 3 is the correct answer.

questions.q:

questions.solution:

Key Points

• When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly.

• The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it.

• Here, only C is independent and introduces the subject of the passage which deals with an ant which almost drowned.

• It should be followed by A which moves the story forward by talking about how a dove saw the ant in danger and what action the dove took.

• So, A must come after C. Then CA is the correct order.

• This order is only shown in option 3, which shows the full sequence as: CADB.

Thus, the correct sequence is: CADB

questions.q:

C. Although not the longest river, the Rio Grande is the most important river in America.

D. America has several long river systems.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2) i.e., ‘DCBA’.

Key Points

• When arranging sentences, it is easier to order the first few; and then eliminate the options accordingly.

• The first sentence of a paragraph is usually independent and introduces a topic. The second one provides more information about it.

• Here, only C and B are independent and introduce a topic related to the American river system. So, we look at their inter-relation.

• Out of these two, only D is truly independent while C provides more information about one of the rivers in the 'river system' introduced by D.

• So, C must come after D. Then DC is the correct order.

• This order is shown by both options 2 and 4 so, we need to look into the placements of A and B.

• A and B begin with however (an adverb) and but (a conjunction).

• But introduces a sentence that states an opposite viewpoint to what has been stated before.

• Since C states that the Rio Grande is an important river, it should be followed by B which states that it is not used for shipping despite its importance.

• So, B must come after C. Then DCB is the correct order.

• This order is shown in option 2, which shows the full sequence as: DCBA.

Thus, the correct sequence is: DCBA
